title: Two tabs: a Drive popup sign-in saved in one tab at the same moment another tab marks the old popup token spent can be overwritten, so the next load asks for one more reconnect
evidence: Codex re-check R1 on lead A29 (branch claude/a29-drive-spent-token). Sequence: tab A gets a 401 on the old popup token; spendToken (widget-src/src/storage/token-flight.ts) reads the stored grant and finds the old token; before A writes, tab B's popup reconnect saves a new grant (savePopupGrant, drive-popup-grant.ts) under the same log-off id; A then writes the old grant, expired, over B's. Effect: B's page keeps working on its in-memory grant, but the next load finds the expired old grant and shows the reconnect panel: one more reconnect. No record data is touched. The window is one synchronous read-then-write; localStorage gives no lock across tabs. Candidate fix: hold one Web Lock (navigator.locks, name per provider) around savePopupGrant's write and spendToken's read-then-write, with a fallback where navigator.locks is missing; a pin that interleaves a save between the read and the write. Owner: a lead after A29 merges, 2026-11-13
